albums.blurb: Nils Frahm is a Berlin-based pianist and composer on the Erased Tapes label, known for blurring the line between concert-hall piano and analog electronics. Spaces was assembled from two years of concert recordings captured on old reel-to-reel machines and cassette decks, and Frahm describes it as a collage of field recordings rather than a conventional live album. It moves from hushed felt-piano minimalism to pulsing synthesizer builds, and on one piece he plays the piano strings with toilet brushes. The whole record is instrumental.
albums.reception: Pitchfork gave Spaces an honorable mention in its Albums of the Year 2014 and placed its centerpiece "Says" at number 47 on its 100 Best Tracks of 2014.

albums.blurb: Freudian is the Toronto singer's debut studio album, released independently on his own Golden Child Recordings after the EPs Praise Break and Pilgrim's Paradise. It distills his church upbringing into gospel-rooted R&B built on choirs, organ, and slow-burning guitar, with guest turns from Kali Uchis, H.E.R., Syd, and Charlotte Day Wilson, and it remains the record that took him from Toronto's independent scene to international audiences.
albums.reception: Freudian was nominated for Best R&B Album at the 60th Grammy Awards, and its single "Best Part" with H.E.R. won Best R&B Performance at the 61st.

albums.blurb: Jorge Ben is the Rio de Janeiro singer-guitarist who invented samba-rock and wrote "Mas Que Nada," the song Sérgio Mendes made world-famous. África Brasil, his fourteenth album, is the turning point where he traded his acoustic guitar for an electric one, fusing samba rhythms with American funk and soul over a big percussion-heavy band; it opens with the football anthem "Ponta de Lança Africano (Umbabarauma)" and includes "Taj Mahal," whose melody Rod Stewart lifted for "Da Ya Think I'm Sexy?" before settling out of court.
albums.reception: África Brasil is featured in the reference book 1001 Albums You Must Hear Before You Die and is the subject of its own volume in Bloomsbury's 33 1/3 book series on landmark albums.
